part: 12-way (2x6) 1.27mm shrouded IDC header, keyed, right-angle, through-hole
description: Key chain connector - one at each end of each key board's IDC ribbon (CBL-CHAIN), on the main board and on the key board
package: THROUGH-HOLE right-angle, 2x6, 1.27mm pitch - envelope config/body.yaml boards.chain_hdr_*
notes: Quantity is the tracked figure chain-connectors; do not restate it. STAND-IN: Samtec SHF-106-01-L-D-RA [datasheets/connectors/SAMTEC-SHF-1.27MM-SHROUDED-IDC-HEADER.pdf - catalogue page; the full print is not banked]. THROUGH-HOLE, so the cable's pull goes into the board, not into SMT pads. PINOUT, NUMBERED AT THE MAIN-BOARD END: 1 GND, 2 SCK, 3 GND, 4 SH/LD, 5 GND, 6 SER, 7 GND, 8 QH, 9 GND, 10 3V3, 11 spare, 12 spare - a ground between every signal in the ribbon (ADR 0001 item 1). Pin 6 is the key board's own serial input and pin 8 its own serial output, on both ribbons, so both key boards are wired alike. THE SAME PART AT ALL FOUR POSITIONS: standing on the main board's top, and on each key board hanging from its underside directly over the main board's, both mouths facing the same way along the body, in the far band beside the LED strip (mechanical/DESIGN.md). *** THE KEY BOARD'S PIN NUMBERS ARE NOT THE MAIN BOARD'S: main-board pin n arrives at key-board pin 12-n for odd n and 14-n for even n. *** KEY-BOARD PINOUT: 12 SCK, 10 SH/LD, 8 SER, 6 QH, 4 3V3, 3/5/7/9/11 GND, 1 and 2 spare. Net the key board's J-CHAIN by that map and place the standard footprint on the bottom side - do not hand-mirror it [calc, key-chain-loom.md]. OPEN UNTIL THE FULL PRINT CONFIRMS standard IDC numbering (odd pins one row, even the other, 1 and 2 at the same end) and where the key sits. The key board's header pin tails come up through the board toward the grounded key plate: the plate has a window over them (mechanical/DESIGN.md). Placed clear of the switches by mechanical/drc.echo 'chain headers on the left_hand boards clear of the switches' and its right_hand rule. OPEN, DECIDED AT M4: the part number, with its full print

part: 12-conductor 1.27mm IDC flat ribbon cable assembly, 2x6 IDC socket each end
description: Key chain ribbon - one per key board, main board to key board, folded closed as a flat hairpin along the body
notes: One per key board (PCB-CLUSTER): the key chain's only conductors off the main board. STAND-IN: Samtec FFSD-06-D, bought as an assembled length [datasheets/connectors/SAMTEC-FFSD-1.27MM-IDC-CABLE.pdf - catalogue page]. STRAIGHT THROUGH: conductor n is socket position n at both ends and main-board J-CHAIN pin n; J-CHAIN's key-board pinout carries the change of order. Both sockets plug in from the same side, because both headers' mouths face the same way. LENGTH: mechanical/drc.echo 'key-chain ribbon length (derived)' - order that length or the next stock one up. It lets the lid lie face down beside the body off its far edge with both sockets plugged in (config/body.yaml routing.chain_service). CLOSED: a flat hairpin along the body, its legs one at each plug's height, so it never stands across the LED strip's light (drc.echo 'key-chain ribbon closed: hairpin leg and fold radius'); the left hand's folds toward the tail, the right hand's toward the mouth (routing.chain_fold). Width and thickness: routing.chain_ribbon_w and routing.chain_ribbon_t. TO TAKE THE LID OFF: lift it, lay it beside the body, unplug both sockets. OPEN, DECIDED AT M4: the part number and stock length

description: Series damping at the chain driving end on SCK, SH/LD and the chain-end SER
notes: On the main board where the MCU's pins arrive, before anything else on the net. SCK and SH/LD each reach four 74HC165s: right_thumb and left_thumb on the main board, and one at the far end of each key board's ribbon, over up to the main board's length (mechanical/drc.echo 'main board (derived)'). At that length an MCU edge sees a line rather than a lump [calc, key-chain-loom.md]. Edge-rate damping at the source - NOT series termination, which ADR 0001 rejected (as R-TERM-CHAIN) for a line that drops on four registers. Same 100R as R-SPI-SER. OPEN, DECIDED AT E14: scope SCK at the left_hand register on the real main board and ribbons; fit if it rings through the 74HC165 thresholds. Three 0805s either way

description: ESD protection on the MCU pins the key chain brings to the main board's ribbon headers
notes: FIT IT (ADR 0018). Channels: SCK, SH/LD and the chain-end SER (IO38, IO7, IO33, each on the connector side of its R-CHAIN-SER); the fourth is spare. The chain's QH into the MCU (IO40) comes from right_thumb on the main board and reaches no connector. Return to GND_CHAIN, the main board's ground pour. WHY: with the lid off and a socket unplugged, a main-board J-CHAIN header exposes three MCU pins behind 100R to a hand - and the sockets are plugged in every time the lid goes back on. It cannot be added once the board is made, and it costs pennies. PLACE IT at the left_hand J-CHAIN, which carries all three channels; SCK and SH/LD reach the right_hand J-CHAIN on the same nets. PACKAGE: SP0504BAHTG is SOT23-5 with 4 CH per the banked SP0504BAHT.pdf p.1 ordering table; SOT23-6 is SP0505BAHTG with 5 CH. All channels share one common pin. It and U-TVS-SPI are two packages because each clamps at its own connector, and J-UMB and the J-CHAIN are at different places on the main board

part: Ferrite bead 600R @ 100MHz or more, DCR 0.1R or less, rated 0.5A or more
description: Series isolation on the 3V3 conductor of each key board's ribbon, on the main board
notes: ONE PER RIBBON, in series between the main board's 3V3 (DEV_3V3 - the Matrix's ME6217C33M5G LDO, reaching the main board on CBL-MCU-RIBBON) and that ribbon's conductor 10 (main-board J-CHAIN pin 10). right_thumb, left_thumb and R-SER-TERM stay on DEV_3V3 directly. IT IS ISOLATION, NOT PROTECTION: it keeps a key board's register edges off the rail that is also the MCP3202's reference. SHORT-CIRCUIT PROTECTION IS THE LDO'S OWN (ADR 0018): datasheets/discrete-and-power/ME6217C33M5G.pdf p.1 'a built-in overcurrent protector' and thermal shutdown at 160C; p.4 Ishort 350mA TYPICAL at VOUT = 0V, with no min or max. The short to expect is a socket forced or a ribbon pinched across conductors 9/10 (main-board J-CHAIN pins 9/10) at reassembly: the whole 3V3 rail collapses, the Matrix does not start, and it is seen on the bench before the lid is closed. VERIFY AT E1: short one ribbon's 3V3 to GND through 1 ohm at J-CHAIN, confirm the rail limits and the Matrix restarts when it is removed. RATINGS: rated current at or above 0.5A, because the bead carries the LDO's limit (350mA typ) for as long as a short lasts [calc]. DCR 0.1R or less: at the chain's whole 27.3mA (19 closed keys at 1.43mA) that is 2.7mV at most [calc]. CHECK AT E14: the bead and the key board's C-DECOUPLE-165 (100nF) form an LC near 0.5MHz if the bead is ~1uH below its resistive band [calc, bead inductance from memory], close to the chain's clock; scope the key board's VCC while shifting and add a damping bulk cap on the key board if it rings. PART NUMBER OPEN [from memory: 0805 beads meeting all three figures are a stock family]

description: Pull-up on the chain-end serial input, on the main board
notes: left_hand's SER, which leaves on conductor 6 of its ribbon (main-board J-CHAIN pin 6, key-board pin 8). ON THE MAIN BOARD at that ribbon's J-CHAIN, on the connector side of R-CHAIN-SER - so the two key boards stay identical. Holds the chain-end input high when nothing drives it, which is the tied-off case ADR 0001 specified. If firmware DRIVES it from IO33, the 100R series wins against 10k to within 33mV of the rail (3.3V x 100/10100) - so an end-to-end self-test (shift a known pattern through all 32 bits, and through both ribbons in both directions) is a FIRMWARE choice rather than a board choice. Fit it. Whether firmware uses it is decided at E4
